scenarios.prompt: Write a TypeScript function that looks up a user by ID from a Map<string, User>. Handle the case where the user doesn't exist. Do not return null or undefined.
criteria: Uses Option.from(), Option.some(), or Option.none() (or the equivalent some()/none()/toOption() functions) instead of null/undefined
Does not return null or undefined directly from the function
Uses .match() or .orElse() to handle the absent case at the call site

scenarios.prompt: Write TypeScript: given a user ID, get the user from a cache (Map<string, User>), then get their profile (Map<string, Profile>), then get their avatar URL (profile.avatarUrl may be undefined). Each step may return nothing. Chain these safely without nested null checks.
criteria: Uses .bind() or .bindAsync() to chain optional steps (.map() is also acceptable for reading a field that may be undefined, since map turns null/undefined into none)
Does not use nested if/null checks between steps
The chain stops at the first absent value without explicit branching

scenarios.prompt: Express + Redis + Prisma app. Write an async function that gets a session token from Redis (returns string | null), validates it to get a user ID (async, may return null), then loads the user from Prisma (may return null). Return a 404 response if any step returns nothing.
criteria: Uses Option for absent values instead of null checks
Uses Option.fromAsync() and/or .bindAsync() for the async optional steps
Produces the 404/success response with .match() or .orElse() on the async Option chain (these return a Promise there), or with .matchAsync()/.orElseAsync()
